feedback: The current geometry with 7 sensors spaced across the front and a larger sensor size of 0.016 provides good line detection resolution and stable turning due to the wide wheel track of 0.15. This geometry helped by giving the controller rich sensor data and stable physical footing. However, the robot still went off track early in both oval and s-bend trials, indicating the controller had to compensate for insufficient steering precision and oscillations rather than geometry limitations. The integrator had to reduce base speed and adjust PID gains to improve control. To further help the controller, please consider trying a slightly narrower wheel track (e.g., 0.14) to allow quicker turning response without sacrificing too much stability, and/or a slightly smaller sensor size (0.012) to reduce sensor overlap and improve edge detection sharpness. These changes could help the controller by balancing stability and agility and improving sensor signal clarity.
requested_changes: wheel_track: 0.14 to improve turning agility while maintaining stability
sensor_size: 0.012 to reduce sensor overlap and sharpen line edge detection
